label: rem:symmetry-preserving-leptons
title: Symmetry-preserving versus symmetry-broken lepton generators
html:
Remark. Symmetry-preserving versus symmetry-broken lepton generators

Remark. The classification of prop:s5-equivariant-torus-knots admits a sharp physical reading. The three charged lepton generations map to torus knots:

  \text{electron} \;=\; T_{2,3},
  \qquad
  \text{muon} \;=\; T_{2,5},
  \qquad
  \text{tau} \;=\; T_{2,7}.

Under pure topological embedding (Seifert genus \leq 4), all three fit on Bring's surface. Under the stronger equivariant criterion—preserving the knot's intrinsic cyclic symmetry along the embedding—the proposition cuts the list to two:

Particle Knot Cyclic symmetry \mathbb{Z}_s \hookrightarrow S_5? Embedding
electron T_{2,3} \mathbb{Z}_3 yes (3-cycle) symmetry-preserving
muon T_{2,5} \mathbb{Z}_5 yes (5-cycle) symmetry-preserving
tau T_{2,7} \mathbb{Z}_7 no (no order-7 element in S_5) symmetry-broken
(ghost) T_{2,9} \mathbb{Z}_9 no (no order-9 element) symmetry-broken, saturates g=4
(ghost) T_{2,11} \mathbb{Z}_{11} no doubly excluded (g = 5 > 4)

Reading. The electron and muon are the only leptons whose cyclic rotational symmetry is realized by a genuine element of \mathrm{Aut}(\Sigma_4) = S_5. The tau embeds topologically by virtue of its genus (g(T_{2,7}) = 3 \leq 4) but fails equivariance: its \mathbb{Z}_7 symmetry is not a subgroup of S_5. The tau is a lepton in the topological spectrum, but not in the symmetry spectrum.

Physical consequence. If lepton-generation structure derives from the cyclic symmetry of a \Sigma_4-embedded torus knot, the equivariant criterion predicts exactly two generations of charged leptons. Three generations are observed, matching the topological-embedding criterion. The equivariant proposition sharpens this: tau carries its mass because the symmetry-broken embedding still admits a Seifert surface, not because an S_5-compatible cyclic structure exists. This aligns with the weight-identification picture (rem:weight-identification-consequences), where the electron and muon representations fit into the \mathbb{Z}_5-graded structure of the \mathcal{X}_5 substrate.

Scope. The proposition does not prohibit the tau. It dictates that the tau requires a different mechanism (symmetry-broken embedding) than the electron and muon (symmetry-preserving embedding). The genus saturation at T_{2,9} excludes fourth and higher generations. The three-generation structure is 2 + 1, not 3 + 0.
